thread.title: Why AT&T Could lose NFL Sunday Ticket Rights To Apple, Amazon, Google | Investor's Business Daily

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Why AT&T Could lose NFL Sunday Ticket Rights To Apple, Amazon, Google | Investor's Business Daily
text:
AT&T 's ( T ) DirecTV could lose its rights to NFL Sunday Ticket to the likes of Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ) or Alphabet ( GOOGL )-unit Google as soon as the 2020 football season, two analysts say.
X The tech giants could swoop in to grab the rights to broadcast all National Football League Sunday afternoon games, since the NFL can exercise a clause to renegotiate a new deal after this year's Super Bowl in February, says BTIG analyst Richard Greenfield.
"We believe the NFL will trigger the option as the Sunday Ticket package enables them to attract a technology platform bidder that will not impact the league's reach," Greenfield said in a blog published on Wednesday.
Greenfield echoed a note last week from Cowen & Co. analyst Colby Synesael, who also said AT&T could lose the rights to NFL Sunday Ticket. He says Amazon's streaming of NFL Thursday night games has been a plus for the e-commerce giant.

Please contact customer service CLOSE "With a shrinking satellite base, choppy NFL ratings, improved quality of live sports streaming, and premier content being bid up by deep-pocketed new entrants, we believe the NFL could rescind its current agreement as it looks for more reach and to tap a wider addressable market," Synesael said.
NFL Sunday Ticket As Promo Tool Rights to NFL Sunday games have been a big promotional tool for satellite TV broadcaster DirecTV. Analysts estimate about 10% of DirecTV subscribers buy the NFL Sunday package. AT&T acquired DirecTV for $49 billion in mid-2015.
DirecTV renewed its NFL Sunday Ticket rights in 2014. An eight-year deal runs through 2022, but the league can opt out early under terms of the deal.
DirecTV pays $1.5 billion annually for the rights. Like other professional sports leagues, the NFL has preferred traditional broadcasters to carry games. CBS ( CBS ), Comcast's ( CMCSA ) NBC, Walt Disney's ( DIS ) ABC and Fox ( FOX ) usually get the nod because of their audience reach.
"While the NFL refused to sell Sunday Ticket to the highest bidder last time (Google), we believe they are far more willing to embrace a tech platform this time around," added Greenfield. "While our gut instinct is that Amazon will be the winner, we would not be shocked to see Apple or Google/YouTube acquire the rights."
Apple plans to launch a video streaming service for TV and movies in 2019.
Amazon Bidding For Sports Networks? Amazon reportedly is among the bidders for regional sports networks up for sale at 21st Century Fox Entertainment ( FOXA ). Walt Disney ( DIS ) is expected to close its purchase of Fox media assets soon. Regulators are requiring the sale of regional sports networks as a condition to approve the deal.
If AT&T loses rights to NFL Sunday Ticket, the timing could be bad. AT&T lost 359,000 DirecTV subscribers in the September quarter. DirecTV had 19.62 million subscribers as of Sept. 30, down a million from 20.6 million a year earlier.
"We believe Apple, Amazon, or (Disney's) ESPN Plus would be an ideal home," added Synesael. "That said, losing the NFL Sunday Ticket may not be a bad thing for AT&T. While AT&T does not disclose specific subscriber or financial metrics, it's been reported that AT&T does not make a profit on the deal in isolation, and instead makes up for it on subscription fees and other upsells."
AT&T stock fell 2.2% to close at 30.10 on the stock market today ; it dropped 26% overall during 2018. However, AT&T stock has gained in nine of the last 10 trading sessions amid analyst upgrades.
